name: Nanotube flywheel
subtitle: a spinning grid battery that never wears out

effects.effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal

effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal
how: Wind and solar need storage that lasts decades, and chemical batteries fade after a few thousand cycles. A rotor wound from nanotube fibre, many times stronger than steel for its weight, spins at enormous speed in a vacuum and holds as much energy per kilogram as a lithium battery; a motor spins it up to charge and works as a generator to give the power back, for millions of cycles.
obstacle: Long nanotube fibres are still about ten times weaker than single nanotubes, which wipes out most of the gain.
why: Carbon-fibre flywheels exist; nanotube rotors remain on paper.
real: CNT-reinforced flywheel rotors appear in patents, a Navy SBIR proposal and Sandia studies; no CNT-fibre rotor prototype found.
